# Listing Loaded Modules (Shared Libraries)

## The Command

```bash
ldd /path/to/executable -v
```

Or for a running process:

```bash
cat /proc/[PID]/maps | grep -E 'lib|\.so'
```

## What the `-v` Flag Does

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `-v` (verbose) | Shows the **full path** to each shared library and its **version**, rather than just the library name. It also shows the **address** where each library is loaded in memory. |

### Example Output

```
$ ldd /usr/bin/ls -v
    linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007fffc6d4f000)
    libselinux.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libselinux.so.1 (0x00007f8a1234567)
    libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007f8a1234500)
    libpthread.so.0 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0 (0x00007f8a1234400)
    ...
```

---
